title: Layout editor: choose the structure
question: The look stays Console System Menu (pale blue, white panels, navy, rounded type). These are three ways to arrange the editor window. Lock one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Layers rail + inspector by the selection
options.thesis: A list of every element on the left, the canvas in the middle, and the selected element's X/Y/W/H in a small card right next to it.
options.viewport: Top bar: layout name, Undo/Redo, Snap 8 px, canvas size, Cancel/Save. Left: element list grouped Stick / Face / Shoulders / D-pad / Extras, each with a show/hide eye. Center: the canvas at 150% with handles on the selection and a floating number card beside it.
options.risk: The floating card can cover the element next to the one you're editing; it has to dodge to the free side.

options.label: Element tiles + footer inspector
options.thesis: Elements picked from a whole-cell grid of their real icons, like the Button set grid in settings; numbers live in one footer strip.
options.viewport: Top bar as before. Canvas large on the left. Right column: a 3-wide grid of element cells showing each button's art; a hidden element's cell is struck through; pressing a button on the pad lights its cell. Footer: selected element name, X Y W H fields, Show toggle.
options.risk: The icon grid is tall with 21 elements; the stick, toon and text need non-icon cells.

options.label: Canvas first, drawer for the list
options.thesis: The canvas owns the window at 200%; hidden elements stay on it as dashed ghosts you can click; the element list is a drawer you open when needed.
options.viewport: Thin top toolbar. The canvas at 200% fills the window. A bottom strip shows the selection: name, X Y W H, Show, size lock. An Elements (21) button opens a right drawer with the list.
options.risk: Dashed ghosts add clutter when many elements are hidden; the list is one click away.
